title: Mix Quiz 03 — Normalisation and Oracle SQL Practical
description: Applied practice in normalisation, keys, Oracle constraints, datatypes and row filtering.

items.question: Mary has two results for MT02: grade F in semester 1 and grade C in semester 3. Assume a student can have at most one result per subject per semester. Which composite key identifies each result?
items.explanation: The same student–subject pair can recur. Semester distinguishes attempts, while both IDs identify whose result and which subject.

items.question: PERSONS has primary key PersonID and contains only P01. ORDERS has a foreign key PersonID referencing PERSONS. Which proposed non-NULL PersonID can be inserted into an otherwise valid order?
items.explanation: A non-NULL foreign key must match an existing parent key; only P01 exists.

items.question: Tweedy (PetID 519) received procedures 20 and 12 on 30 April 2021. A report stores one row per procedure performed. Why is (PetID, VisitDate) not a valid primary key for this report?

options.text: Both rows have different pet IDs
The pair includes the procedure code

items.explanation: The pet and date repeat even though the procedures differ, so the pair does not uniquely identify a row.

items.question: PRODUCT contains B-100 (quantity 10), S-201 (300), N-122 (400) and B-101 (50). Which IDs remain after DELETE FROM product WHERE quantity > 280?
items.explanation: DELETE removes the rows that satisfy the filter. Quantities 10 and 50 do not satisfy it, so their rows remain.

items.question: COURSE(CID, CName, School, SCEXT) has primary key CID. Each course belongs to one school, and each school has one extension (SCEXT). Which decomposition preserves all facts and removes the transitive dependency?
items.explanation: School determines SCEXT. Keeping School in COURSE preserves the link, while storing SCEXT in SCHOOL removes the indirect dependency from COURSE.

items.question: In the PERSONS table, Age has CHECK (Age >= 0 AND Age <= 120) and NOT NULL. With all other columns valid, which Age is accepted?
items.explanation: 120 meets the inclusive upper bound. NULL violates NOT NULL, and −1 and 121 are outside the allowed range.

items.question: Each product has one price regardless of colour. Product 1 costs 15.99 and comes in red and green. Which design stores each colour separately without duplicating the product price?

options.text: PRODUCT(ProductID, Colour, Price), one row per colour

items.explanation: Store the price once per product and one colour per PRODUCT_COLOUR row. A list or numbered columns keep a repeating group; a flat row per colour repeats the price.

items.question: POSTS has primary key PostID and CATEGORIES has primary key CategoryID. PostCategories(PostID, CategoryID) allows many categories per post and many posts per category, but no duplicate pair. Which constraints implement these rules?

options.text: A primary key on PostID and a foreign key on CategoryID only
Separate UNIQUE constraints on both columns plus both foreign keys
A composite primary key on both columns but no foreign keys
A composite primary key on both columns plus a foreign key from each column to its parent

items.explanation: The composite key prevents repeated pairs without blocking either ID from appearing in other pairs. The two foreign keys ensure both parent rows exist.

items.question: A FreshMart receipt has one cashier. Assume CashierID determines CashierName, and the same cashier can issue many receipts. Which design preserves the cashier link without repeating the cashier name on every receipt?

options.text: RECEIPT(ReceiptNo) and CASHIER(CashierID, CashierName) with no link

items.explanation: Store the name once with its determinant, CashierID. Keeping CashierID in RECEIPT identifies who issued each receipt.

items.question: The STUDENT practical requires DOB to store an actual date and CGPA to store a numeric value with one decimal place. Which Oracle column definitions meet those requirements and can store a CGPA of 3.2?
items.explanation: DATE represents a date, and NUMBER(2,1) has two total digits with one after the decimal point, so it can store 3.2.
